MediaStr.menuSub: Convert audio, image and video formats, and text encoding
MediaStr.mixSub: Convert and compress audio, images and video together from one folder
MediaStr.mixIntro: Pick one folder that holds a mix of audio, images and video. The app groups files by extension, and each type uses its own rules (output format, compression and Advanced Settings, same as the Audio, Image and Video converters). Tap a type's title to open its rules; the switch on the right decides whether that type is processed. Switched-off types are left untouched, and types missing from the folder are disabled automatically. Audio and images are processed first, video last (one at a time). In Overwrite Originals mode files whose format stays the same are replaced in place, while files whose format changes produce a new file next to them. The Text and Special converters are not included.
MediaStr.mixScan: Folder contents: Audio {0} files ({1}) · Images {2} files ({3}) · Video {4} files ({5}) · Unrecognized {6} files
MediaStr.mixCopyOthers: Copy unrecognized files as they are
MediaStr.mixCopyHint: Off by default: files that are not audio, images or video are skipped and do not appear in the output folder. When checked, they are copied unchanged into the output folder (folder structure kept) so the result folder is complete. Not used in Overwrite Originals mode because the originals are already in place.
MediaStr.mixNoneNote: No files of this type in the folder
MediaStr.mixNothing: Enable at least one type (Audio, Images or Video) or copy unrecognized files.

MediaStr.folderEmpty: No matching files in this folder.
MediaStr.fmtMissing: The selected format is not available in the folder
MediaStr.folderInputHint: If the folder contains files of different formats, change Input format to choose which files are converted. The subfolder structure is kept in the output folder.
MediaStr.folderTypes: Folder: only {0} files. The subfolder structure is kept in the output folder.
MediaStr.extFilterHint: Separate with commas. Required, so binary files are not touched.
MediaStr.conflict: If the result file already exists
MediaStr.bgNote: Recommended: enable "Background processing" and "Keep screen on while running" in Settings.
MediaStr.formatNA: Output format not available, please choose manually!
MediaStr.compOver: The entered size exceeds the source file size!
MediaStr.compHint: Quality: 100% = no compression. Size: each result is tuned to be close to that number (approximate). If the output format differs, the file is converted and compressed in one pass. Files already smaller than the target are not compressed.
MediaStr.busyNote: A process is running, please cancel it first
MediaStr.cancelRunConfirm: Cancel the running conversion? Files already converted are kept; the file being processed is not written.
MediaStr.discardHint: This button appears when some results are larger than their source files (this can happen with OGG (Vorbis) compression, conversion to WAV/FLAC, or any other format that is simply bigger). Pressing it deletes those larger result files. If a result replaced the original and a backup exists in _backup, the original is restored. Results without a backup cannot be discarded and are left as they are. Source files are never deleted.
MediaStr.discardConfirm: {0} result files larger than their sources will be deleted (or the originals restored from _backup if the results replaced them). This cannot be undone.
MediaStr.backConfirm: A process is running. Cancel it and go back?
MediaStr.onlyOverHint: Files equal to or smaller than this limit are not compressed (still converted if the format differs).
MediaStr.vorbisFloorNote: OGG (Vorbis) cannot go below about 50 kbps (stereo), so sources that are already low-bitrate will not shrink and the result can be larger. Results larger than the source can be removed with the Discard larger results button after the process finishes. For smaller files choose OGG (Opus) or M4A.
MediaStr.estimateNote: Rough estimate; the actual size may differ.
MediaStr.audCompressHint: Quality: AAC/Opus/MP3/Vorbis bitrate is multiplied by the percentage (WAV and FLAC: lower sample rate). Size: bitrate is calculated from the target (WAV and FLAC: lower sample rate and channels; a FLAC result may end up smaller than the target).
MediaStr.imgCompressHint: Quality: JPG/WEBP use the slider value as quality; PNG becomes a palette PNG (color count = slider × 256, transparency kept). Size: quality/color count is searched automatically until the result is near the target.
MediaStr.imgQualityHint: PNG and lossless WEBP ignore quality (always lossless).
MediaStr.imgNote: EXIF orientation is applied automatically. For animated GIFs only the first frame is used.
MediaStr.vidFormatHint: Encoders come from the device. H.265 and VP9 are not on every device; if missing, the file is marked as failed. WebM needs Android 10+ to keep its audio (Opus).
MediaStr.vidCompressHint: Quality: the video bitrate is multiplied by the percentage. Size: the bitrate is calculated from the target and the Video Bitrate choice is ignored.
MediaStr.vidNote: Resolution is only reduced (never enlarged) and frame rate only lowered. AAC audio is copied without re-encoding; other audio is encoded to AAC 128 kbps.
MediaStr.txtNote: Files that are already UTF-8 (or already in the target encoding) keep their content and count as "unchanged". Shift-JIS uses CP932 (windows-31j), which includes the Windows extra characters.
MediaStr.presetSave: Save these settings as a preset
MediaStr.presetHint: A preset stores all settings of this converter (except the source files and folders).
MediaStr.sampleOn: Create a sample and compare with the source
MediaStr.sampleHint: Converts one file (the first in the folder) with the current settings and shows a before/after comparison (audio is playable). Nothing is written to your folders; processing all files still starts from the Start Conversion button.
MediaStr.inPlaceHint: Folder mode only. Results are written into the source folder. If the result has the same name, the original is backed up first to a _backup folder inside the source folder; if the extension changes, the original is kept and the result is added next to it.
MediaStr.resUndoHint: Undo = delete the result file, or restore the original from _backup if the result replaced it.
MediaStr.audNormHint: Evens out loudness across files (RMS): Light -20 dB, Medium -16 dB, Loud -12 dB. Peaks are limited to -1 dB to avoid clipping. Needs an extra scan pass, so it takes a bit longer.
MediaStr.audTrim: Trim silence at start and end
MediaStr.audLoopHint: Loop tags are read from the source OGG, adjusted for sample rate/trimming, and written to the result OGG. The tags are written to both OGG (Vorbis) and OGG (Opus). The built-in RPGM MV/MZ loop reader understands OGG Vorbis tags, so choose OGG (Vorbis) for looping BGM.
MediaStr.imgMultipleHint: For tilesets/spritesheets so sizes stay grid-aligned (e.g. 48). Applies to Percent and Size resolution; never exceeds the source size.
MediaStr.imgDither: Dithering when PNG colors are reduced
MediaStr.overwriteHow: Results are written straight into the source folder. If a result has the same name as the original, the original is overwritten; when ticked, the original is first copied to a _backup folder inside the source folder (clashing names get (1)). If the extension changes, the original is kept and the result is added next to it.
MediaStr.backupWarn: Warning: without a backup the originals are overwritten permanently and the result cannot be undone. Make sure you have another copy.
MediaStr.audTrimHint: Silence at the start and end (below about -50 dBFS) is removed, leaving a 10 ms margin. The middle of the file is untouched. Handy for SE/BGM with blank gaps; the result gets shorter and loop tags are adjusted automatically.
MediaStr.imgDitherHint: When PNG colors are reduced (Quality below 100%), color error is spread to neighboring pixels so gradients (skin, sky, shadows) look smooth without color bands, but slightly noisy and the file can be several times larger than without dithering. Good for gradient images; leave it off for pixel art.
MediaStr.specialSub: Convert special media formats from several engines
MediaStr.specialIntro: Pick .pcm (XPCM) and/or .crx files extracted from Circus archives (PCK/CRM). The type is recognised by extension and the result keeps the name with the new extension.
MediaStr.spAudioHint: Automatic: XPCM containing Ogg Vorbis becomes the original .ogg untouched (quality and loop tags kept), anything else becomes .wav. Always WAV: Ogg is decoded with Android's decoder first. Supported: Ogg, raw PCM and ADPCM; old MDCT-compressed XPCM (modes 1 and 3) is not supported yet and is reported as failed.
MediaStr.spImageHint: CRX images become .png (24-bit, 32-bit with alpha, or paletted). Differential CRX (CRXD, e.g. facial expressions) is merged with its base image automatically; the base file must be selected/present in the same folder (its name is stored in the file). Zstd-compressed CRX (newer versions) is not supported yet.
MediaStr.spEngineIntro: Pick .crx, .pgd, .pna and/or .pcm (XPCM) files extracted from Circus archives. The type is recognised by extension and the result keeps the name with the new extension. Differential CRX (CRXD) and differential PGD need their base file selected too (same folder). PNA (AdvHD) is an atlas of several images.
MediaStr.spEngineIntro#2: Pick .pgd files. Support uses the documented PGD decoder (Softpal family: GE, PGD3, PGD2). No public source for an Artemis-specific PGD variant was found; unrecognised files are reported as failed.
MediaStr.spEngineIntro#3: Pick .ovk files. Each OVK holds many Ogg Vorbis streams, so the result is one .zip of the .ogg files (untouched). The entry table is validated against the file size because OVK has no signature.
MediaStr.spEngineIntro#4: Pick .hg2/.hg3 files extracted from CatSystem2 archives. Layers/frames are composed onto the full canvas. HG-3 containing JPEG is decoded with Android's decoder.
MediaStr.spEngineIntro#5: Pick .eri (image), .mio (Entis audio) and/or .emi files. ERI images: lossless paths only (RunLength, Huffman, Nemesis). MIO audio: lossless and lossy (LOT) ported from GARbro/vgmstream, but the lossy path is completely untested. Honest note: in GARbro .emi is actually an Entis image (EMSAC), not audio, so .emi files are reported as failed.
MediaStr.spEngineIntro#6: Pick .tlg (TLG0/5/6 images), .ovk (Ogg container, .zip result) and/or .mio (MIO audio) files.
MediaStr.spEngineIntro#7: Pick .rct and .rc8 files. The RC8 paired with an RCT (named "<name>_.rc8") is used automatically as the alpha channel when selected in the same folder; a standalone RC8 is converted as a paletted image.
MediaStr.spEngineIntro#8: Pick .spm files. Honest warning: the documented NeXAS SPM (Karaik/NeXAS_DX) holds a sprite map (image names, hitboxes, animation), not pixel data, so it cannot be turned into PNG yet. Files are reported as failed until a sample proves otherwise.
MediaStr.spEngineIntro#9: Pick .g00 (type 0, 1, 2 images) and/or .nwa (audio) files. G00 type 3 (XOR'd JPEG) is not supported yet.
MediaStr.spEngineIntro#10: Pick .pgd and/or .ycg files. YCG covers method 1 only (two zlib streams); method 2 (YSSnp) is not supported yet. PGD uses the Softpal-family decoder; no Yu-Ris-specific PGD variant exists in the reference sources (the documented Yu-Ris image extension is .ycg).
MediaStr.spAudioHint3: Automatic and Always WAV produce .wav (16-bit PCM). OGG: the decoded audio is encoded to Ogg Vorbis 160 kbps (44.1/48 kHz); if the file holds Ogg inside, that Ogg is copied untouched.
MediaStr.spAllFramesHint: Off: only the first frame/layer becomes a .png. On: all frames are saved in one .zip of numbered PNGs.
MediaStr.spImageNote: All these decoders were written from reference source code (GARbro and other projects) without real sample files; results need testing on each game. Images are saved as 32-bit PNG.

MediaStr.compatNote: General rules (format, file names, image size, text encoding), not a guarantee the game will run. Engine versions and plugins differ; still test in the game.

NameOptStr.menuSub: Rename files with special characters to safe names and update their references in the game
NameOptStr.noFolder: Pick the Source Folder (the game folder) first.
NameOptStr.intro: This feature prepares a game (especially RPG Maker MV/MZ) before it is built into an APK. APK builders often fail on file names with non-Latin characters (Hanzi, Kana, Hangul, etc.). The File Name Optimizer renames those files and folders to safe (ASCII) names, then updates the game files that refer to the old names (json, js, html, css, txt, ks, rpy, etc.) so the game still finds its assets. How it works: 1) pick the game folder (everything inside is scanned, including subfolders); 2) set the scope and options; 3) press Scan and Preview to see the list of new names and which files will change, without changing anything; 4) press Rename and Update References. Fill in the Backup Folder to keep copies of the original text files that get edited; every rename is also recorded in rename_mapping.json in the Source Folder so it can be reverted with the Restore Original Names button. Files encrypted by RPG Maker (.rpgmvp, .rpgmvo, etc.) are renamed too while File scope = All files with special characters, because references use the same base name.
NameOptStr.scopeOpts#2: Only media assets with special characters
NameOptStr.scopeHint: All files with special characters: every file (and folder, if included) whose name has non-ASCII characters is renamed, including RPG Maker encrypted files (.rpgmvp, .rpgmvo, .png_, .ogg_), data, plugins and others. Only media assets: only images, audio and video (png, jpg, webp, ogg, m4a, mp3, wav, mp4, webm, etc.) are renamed; other files are left alone.
NameOptStr.styleOpts: Keep the ASCII part (戦闘BGM → BGM_001)
NameOptStr.styleHint: Keep the ASCII part: Latin letters and digits from the old name are reused, followed by a serial number (BGM_戦闘01 → BGM_01_001); if there are none, file_001 is used. The same name in different folders gets the same new name, so references stay consistent. Numbers are skipped when they clash with existing files.
NameOptStr.chkSymbols: Include ASCII names with spaces or special marks
NameOptStr.symbolsHint: Off by default. When checked, names that use only Latin letters but contain spaces or marks such as & # % ' ( ) ! are renamed too (marks become _, e.g. "Actor 1.png" → "Actor_1.png").
NameOptStr.refHint: Safe (recommended): a name is replaced only when it stands whole as a value, for example "背景", "背景.png", "img/pictures/背景", storage=背景.png, including \u80cc\u666f and %E8%83%8C forms which are decoded first. Dialogue text that happens to contain the same word is not touched. Wide: every occurrence of the name (2+ characters) is replaced anywhere, like the original script; useful when the game builds names from pieces of text, but it may also change dialogue or character names that are the same. Check the Preview before using this mode.
NameOptStr.caseHint: Android is case-sensitive, Windows is not. Games from Windows often call Bgm1.ogg while the file is bgm1.ogg, so the asset fails to load in the APK. When checked, references that differ from the real file name only in letter case are corrected (Safe mode only). Ambiguous names (two files that differ only in case) are skipped. This fix is not reverted by Restore Original Names; use a Backup Folder if you want to be able to recover it.

ScriptStr.note#2: Text is taken raw as in the .rpy (\n, \" and {i} tags kept). Decompile the .rpyc first if there is no .rpy.
ScriptStr.note#3: ".ks" scripts: each text line (inline tags such as [r] [p] included) becomes one entry; do not change or remove tags. ".scn" (PSB) scripts: speaker names, messages and choices; newline = real newline. If the file already has an extra language slot, the translation goes to the last slot; otherwise the original text is overwritten.
ScriptStr.note#4: Text lines, speaker names (#name) and [glink] button texts are collected. Do not change or remove tags.
ScriptStr.note#5: Text lines and select choices are taken from the decoded 0.txt. Pick the encoding that matches the game.
ScriptStr.note#6: Dialogue lines ([n] = line break, keep it) and ^select choices are taken from text .s scripts. Pick the encoding that matches the game.
ScriptStr.note#7: All dialogue/narration lines of Artemis .txt files are collected (# names, * labels, [tags] and // comments skipped). Pick the encoding that matches the game. .ast files: dialogue, choices, speaker names and ruby text are collected; tags and file names stay untouched.
ScriptStr.note#8: Dialogue, speaker names and choice command texts are collected from .cst files. Pick the game's encoding (usually Shift-JIS).
ScriptStr.note#9: Dialogue/name/choice texts are collected from SiglusEngine scene .dat files (from an unpacked Scene.pck) by filtering non-ASCII strings, not by bytecode analysis, so a few internal strings may show up. Delete such lines from the export if you do not want them changed.
ScriptStr.note#10: All strings from Escu:de binary scripts (ESCR1_00, unpacked .bin files) are collected; internal resource names are filtered. The string table is rewritten with new offsets on import. Use Shift-JIS for original games.
ScriptStr.note#11: pushstring texts of Favorite/FVP .hcb scripts are collected (ASCII resource names skipped). Jump/call addresses are recomputed on import. Texts over 254 bytes are left unchanged. Use Shift-JIS for original games.
ScriptStr.note#12: Messages, choices and speaker names of WillPlus/AdvHD .ws2 scripts are collected through a disassembler (encrypted files are detected automatically). The %LC/%LF name prefix and %K%P message suffix are preserved; leave other % codes inside texts untouched.
ScriptStr.note#13: Messages and speaker names of Silky Engine .mes scripts (Plus and Ai6Win variants detected automatically). Newline = real newline, ruby = [text]; do not nest [ ] or put newlines inside. Addresses are recomputed on import.
ScriptStr.note#14: Speaker names and messages of Adv32 (Circus) .mes scripts. Latin letters are converted from full-width to ASCII on export and back to full-width on import (the game font has no half-width letters). Newline = real newline. The header offset table is recomputed on import; characters outside Shift-JIS become ？.
ScriptStr.note#15: Messages, names and choices of BGI/Ethornell scripts (V0, V1, and BurikoCompiledScriptVer1.00 with header). Scripts in archives are usually DSC-compressed: unpack with the Decode DSC option first. Changed texts are appended to the file end and pointers redirected. Ruby is left unchanged. Old V0 scripts are not auto-detected: use the BGI engine menu.
ScriptStr.note#16: Yaneurao Itufuru script texts (scanned from text opcodes 0x02 and 0x1E). Lengths are rewritten on import; 0x02 lines must end with a newline (added automatically). Not auto-detected: run via the Itufuru engine menu.
ScriptStr.note#17: Texts (UTF-16) from the conststr section of EntisGLS .csx scripts, version 2.x–3.x; only non-ASCII strings are collected. Scripts come from the NOA archive (script.noa) — Key Finder can find the archive password. CSX 1.x (strings in the image section) is not supported.

The XOR key is read automatically. Import rebuilds the expression section and shifts every offset, so text length is free. The .ybn size changes, so repack the .ypf from the Pack menu.
ScriptStr.note#19: Shift-JIS texts from the text block of NeXAS .bin scripts (Script.pac); only non-ASCII segments are collected. Import rewrites the text block without recalculating offsets — length is free, but test in the game.

AboutStr.how.1.title: Home and Feature Search
AboutStr.how.1.body:
The Home tab is the start page of the app.
• Feature Search: type a feature, engine, or file extension (e.g. "xp3", "tlg", "translate"), then tap a result to open it; its menu path is shown under the title. Tap the star to add it to Favorites.
• Recently used: the features you opened last.
• Quick actions: shortcuts to features. Tap "Edit Quick Actions" to add features by search (up to 10), remove them with the X button, and reorder them by dragging the three-line icon.
• Find features by file: pick a file, then choose a feature that fits its extension; the file is loaded into that feature automatically.
• After opening a feature from Home, the back button always returns you to Home.
• In any search box, the back button or a tap outside the box closes the keyboard and returns the box to its normal look.
AboutStr.how.2.title: Game Assets
AboutStr.how.2.body: With a game-library look that can load several game assets without unpacking the files, as the second tab (after Home). The (+) icon adds a game: pick the game folder, fill in Game Name (auto-filled from the folder name, editable), press Next, then pick an optional cover (if empty, the game icon is used automatically when found) and Add. Search filters the list, Refresh re-checks the folders. The three-dot menu on a card: Rename, Change Cover, Delete Folder (this only removes the list entry, not the real folder or files). Tap a card to open Audio, Images, Video and Text: previews of the game assets with search, sorting, a mini audio player, an image viewer (zoom, swipe), a video player and a text viewer (encoding choice, dialogue extracted from scripts). Encrypted RPG Maker MV/MZ assets are previewed automatically (key from System.json) without changing the original files. Game archives (xp3, rpa, pfs, etc.; every format Unpack Archive supports) are scanned automatically and their contents appear in all four menus with the archive path/file name; audio and video from archives are extracted temporarily to the cache when played. The list is saved so an already scanned game opens instantly without scanning again; folder changes are checked silently in the background and the list is updated only if something changed (the reload button on the game page forces a rescan). Each menu has sorting (name/size, ascending/descending) and pages (Audio and Text 50 files, Images 60, Video 20 per page). The preview cache and its limit (200 MB to 10 GB, default 1 GB) are set in the Settings tab. Below the four menus is an info card (cover, engine, file count, archives read/failed, media loaded/failed; failures are counted as media turn out not to be viewable, e.g. encrypted). Long-press a file, or tap the select-mode icon at the right of "Favorites only", to select several: Extract (to a chosen folder; archive and encrypted files are decrypted), Share (max 20 files / 200 MB) and Favorite; a Favorites only filter is on each list. Internet covers: the cover window has Auto search (VNDB, NextMoe, Steam, then Bing; uses the first result of the first source that has one) and Manual search (search field, source VNDB/NextMoe/Steam/Bing, max 6 results). The cloud icon on the main screen auto-searches covers for all games. The engine label on covers can be turned on in Settings > System Settings (off by default). The sort menu has a Random option: every time it is chosen the list is reshuffled. Auto search always tries VNDB first, then NextMoe, Steam and finally Bing. In every paged list, tap the "Page x / y" label to open "Go to page" and jump straight to a page.
AboutStr.how.3.title: Manage the Game List
AboutStr.how.3.body: Tap the settings icon (two sliders) on the main Game Assets screen to open the list order and three tools: find covers online, add a main folder (every subfolder inside is added as a game at once; ones already listed are skipped), and delete the whole list (only the list; the real folders and files are safe).
AboutStr.how.4.title: Special Asset Converter
AboutStr.how.4.body: In the Media Asset Converter, open "Special Asset Converter" and pick an engine: Adv32 (Circus), Artemis, BGI/Ethornell, CatSystem 2, EntisGLS, Kirikiri, Majiro, NeXAS, Siglus or Yu-Ris. Each engine has converters for its media formats (images to PNG, audio to OGG/WAV; OVK becomes a .zip of .ogg files). All the new decoders were written from reference source code without real samples, so results need testing on the game. Not possible yet: NeXAS SPM (it holds a sprite map, not pixels), YCG method 2, G00 type 3, lossy ERI, and .emi (it is actually an image in GARbro). The lossy MIO path is untested.
AboutStr.how.5.title: Special media formats in Game Assets
AboutStr.how.5.body: Game Assets now also read engine-specific media: .crx, .pgd, .pna, .ycg, .hg2, .hg3, .tlg, .eri, .g00, .rct and .rc8 images show like normal images (tiles, viewer, swipe), and .pcm (XPCM), .nwa, .mio and .ovk audio can be played. Decoded results are kept in a temporary cache. Notes: differential images (CRXD, PGD3, RCT overlay) cannot be previewed because their base file is not looked up; OVK plays only its first entry (use the Special Asset Converter for all of them); Extract/Share still deliver the original file. After updating the app, tap Refresh in the game list so special files are detected.
AboutStr.how.6.title: Quick start
AboutStr.how.6.body:
1. On the Game Tools tab choose RPGM Tools (RPG Maker) or VN Tools (visual novels). The Support Tools tab holds the Translation Editor, Text Editor, File Inspection, File Toolkit and Key Finder; the Settings tab holds settings, Guide, Source and About.
2. Pick a file or folder with the upload card (the Android file picker).
3. Pick an output folder, then press the process button.
4. Watch progress and the log on the same screen; the result is in the output folder.
AboutStr.how.7.title: VN Tools > Unpack Archive
AboutStr.how.7.body:
Extract a visual novel archive.
• Pick the archive. The format is detected automatically and its info (format, file count, supported engines) is shown.
• If the format has options (e.g. filename encoding or XOR key) they appear below. Changing the encoding reloads the file list.
• "View archive contents" browses files and folders with search and image/text Preview.
• "Select files" extracts only part of the archive.
• Pick an output folder and start. Afterwards you get Open Folder, Copy Log and Verify.
• Preview supports images, audio (ogg, mp3, wav, m4a, flac, etc. with play/pause and a seek bar) and text. Long text is split into 50 KB pages with ‹ › buttons and a Copy this page button.
AboutStr.how.8.title: VN Tools > Pack Archive
AboutStr.how.8.body:
Create an archive from a folder.
• Choose the archive format (the engine name is shown). Only writable formats are listed.
• Pick the input folder, enter the output file name and format options (compression, version, encoding, key).
• Fill the ignore filter for files that must not be packed.
AboutStr.how.9.title: Yu-Ris (YPF)
AboutStr.how.9.body: Pick the Yu-Ris engine in the Engine List. Unpack: .ypf (versions 234–500) with names and compressed files. Pack: builds a new .ypf (default version 494, enter 480–500; name/data hashes are computed automatically, .ybn files are compressed). Script Tools: export/import text from ysbin/yst*.ybn scripts (WORD commands and strings inside expressions, Shift-JIS); the XOR key is read automatically and every offset is shifted, so text length is free. Flow: unpack data.ypf/Scripts.ypf → export text → translate → import → repack. Not supported yet: YPF embedded in an .exe, and older scripts (version < 480) were tested only on a v494 sample.
AboutStr.how.10.title: Support Tools > Text Editor > Structured Text
AboutStr.how.10.body: Pick the format you want to edit: JSON, CSV / TSV, INI / CFG, XML or Markdown. All of them use the same Create File / Upload File panel, Output & Result, encoding settings and leave confirmation as Plain Text. The back button in an editor takes you to this format list; XML and Markdown open in a text editor with dedicated highlighting.
AboutStr.how.11.title: Support Tools > Text Editor > Structured Text > JSON
AboutStr.how.11.body:
Edits JSON (e.g. RPG Maker data files) as a tree or as text.
• Tree view: tap an entry holding an object or array to go into it; the path is in the breadcrumb (tap any part, or the ← button, to go up). Tap a plain value to change its key, type (text, number, boolean, null, object, array) and value (a switch for booleans, − and + buttons with a step for numbers). Changing the type converts the value as well as it can.
• The ⋮ menu on each entry: Edit, Duplicate, Move up, Move down, Sort keys (for objects), Copy path (e.g. events[3].pages[0]) and Delete. The Add button creates a new entry at the level you are viewing.
• Find searches keys or values across the whole tree; tap a result to jump to it.
• Text view: a text editor with Find & Replace and a Tidy button. Switching to Tree checks the JSON; if it is invalid, an error message (line and column) appears and you stay in the Text view. An invalid JSON file opens directly in the Text view.
• Key order and number formatting are kept. While the tree is unchanged, the file is saved with its original text. From a changed Tree view the save format can be Pretty (2-space indentation) or Compact (one line) in JSON Settings; from the Text view the file is saved exactly as typed, and only if the JSON is valid.
• The ↶ and ↷ buttons in the Tree view undo and redo tree changes (up to 40 steps, limited by memory).
AboutStr.how.12.title: Support Tools > Text Editor > Structured Text > INI / CFG
AboutStr.how.12.body:
Edits INI, CFG or properties files.
• The first list holds the sections ([name]); keys above the first section go under (global). Tap a section to see its key=value pairs.
• Tap a pair to change its key and value; the ⋮ menu has Edit and Delete. The ＋ New key button adds at the end of the section, and ＋ New section adds a section at the end of the file. The ⋮ menu on a section: Rename section and Delete (with its contents).
• Comments, blank lines, spacing and the original order are not changed; only the lines you change are rewritten. ↶ and ↷ undo and redo (up to 40 steps).
• Only the = sign is recognised as the separator; if your file uses a different format, open it with Plain Text.
AboutStr.how.13.title: Support Tools > Text Editor
AboutStr.how.13.body:
A Support Tools menu between Translation Editor and Media Asset Converter; it holds Plain Text, Structured Text and Bulk Replace.
• Plain Text and Structured Text use the same flow: choose Create File or Upload File, press its button, and the Text Editor Area appears below on the same page (no new editor page).
• Create File: pick a File Format (none for JSON), fill in the Output file name (default text_file), set Output & Result (If the result file already exists and Output Folder), then press Create text file. The button is enabled once the Output Folder is set. The file is created in the Output Folder and opens straight in the editor; Save writes to the same file.
• Upload File: pick a text file (only the formats in the File Format dropdown; other formats show the warning File format not supported), set Output & Result, then press Edit text file. Output & Result offers Output Folder or Overwrite Originals; with Back up ticked, the original is first copied to the _backup folder inside the Output Folder.
• Files over 4 MB are not edited (up to 40 MB they open read-only), and files containing null bytes are treated as not text (use the Hex Viewer in File Inspection).
• Editor Look, encoding and save format are under the Options button in the Text Editor Area. The encoding is detected automatically (BOM, UTF-8, then Shift-JIS) and can be chosen manually, including GBK, Big5, EUC-KR and UTF-16; text that cannot be saved in the chosen encoding is rejected instead of being replaced by question marks.
• Leaving or switching files with unsaved changes shows a confirmation.
• Auto draft: unsaved changes are written to a draft in the app storage 2 seconds after the last change. When the same file is uploaded again you are offered Restore; the draft is deleted after a successful save or when you choose to leave without saving.
AboutStr.how.14.title: Support Tools > Text Editor > Plain Text
AboutStr.how.14.body:
Edits pure text files (.txt, .ini, .cfg, .ks, .rpy, .csv, .xml and similar).
• Choose Create File or Upload File at the top; the editor appears in the Text Editor Area below it.
• The ↶ and ↷ buttons undo and redo (up to 60 steps).
• Find opens the Find & Replace panel: match case, regex (groups can be used in the replace field), Next, the ‹ button for the previous match, Replace and Replace all.
• Line opens a dialog to jump to a line number. Options opens Editor Look, Encoding & Line Endings and Output & Result.
• The symbol bar above the editor inserts hard-to-type characters ({ } [ ] ( ) : ; = < > / # and Tab) at the cursor.
• Syntax highlighting is automatic for JSON, XML/HTML, INI/CFG, .ks, .rpy and Markdown (switched off for text above 300,000 characters). The symbol bar and highlighting can be switched off in Editor Look.
• The status bar shows line, column, character count, encoding and line endings. The title gets a ● mark when there are unsaved changes.
• Save writes according to Output & Result and the chosen encoding.
• Show line numbers and Show spaces, tabs and line ends (a dot · for a space, → for a tab, ¶ for a line end) can be switched on in Editor Look.
• Options > View changes shows the difference between the current text and the text as opened or last saved (added and removed lines).
• Files above 4 MB (up to 40 MB) open read-only, page by page: you can search and copy but not edit or save.
AboutStr.how.15.title: Support Tools > Text Editor > Structured Text > CSV / TSV
AboutStr.how.15.body:
Edits CSV or TSV tables (e.g. translation files).
• The separator (comma, semicolon, tab or pipe) is guessed automatically from the first few lines and can be chosen manually in CSV Settings. Cells containing quotes, separators or line breaks are read correctly.
• The table shows rows and columns in fixed-size cells; scroll sideways for more columns. Tap a cell to edit its contents (multiple lines are allowed). Tap a row number for Insert above or below, Duplicate and Delete; tap a column header for Insert left or right, Delete and Edit header. The ＋ Row and ＋ Column buttons add at the end.
• The first row is treated as the column headers (this can be switched off in CSV Settings; when off, the columns are labelled A, B, C).
• Find searches the text in all cells, then ‹ and › move between results. ↶ and ↷ undo and redo (up to 40 steps).
• While the table is unchanged the file is saved with its original text. Once changed, the quotes used when saving follow your choice: Keep original, When needed or All cells.
• The column header menu also has Sort A → Z and Z → A (numbers are sorted as numbers). Find has two modes: Find (jump between results) and Filter (only the rows containing the text are shown).
• Paste adds the clipboard contents (e.g. rows copied from a spreadsheet, tab-separated) as new rows at the end of the table.
AboutStr.how.16.title: Support Tools > Text Editor > Structured Text > XML and Markdown
AboutStr.how.16.body:
XML and Markdown open in the same text editor as Plain Text (Find & Replace, undo and redo, symbol bar, encoding) with dedicated syntax highlighting.
• XML: Check XML tests whether the document is well-formed and shows the line and column of the first error (the file is not changed). Tidy XML sets 2-space indentation; documents with a DOCTYPE are not tidied so that no data is lost, and spacing inside mixed text can change. A tidy can be undone with undo.
• Markdown: Preview shows a simple rendering (headings, lists, bold, italic, code, links, quotes, rules); press Edit to return to the editor.
• Highlighting is switched off automatically for text above 300,000 characters.
AboutStr.how.17.title: Support Tools > Text Editor > Bulk Replace
AboutStr.how.17.body:
Finds and replaces text across many files in one folder at once.
• Pick the source folder (subfolders optional), the extension filter and the name search to decide which files are checked. Enter the text to find and its replacement; match case and regex (groups can be used in the replace field) are available.
• Count matches checks every file (up to 4 MB, not binary) and lists the files with their number of matches without changing anything.
• Apply to all asks for confirmation, then writes the results according to Output & Result: Output Folder, or Overwrite Originals with Back up to _backup. Each file keeps its encoding and line endings; a file containing characters that cannot be saved in its encoding counts as failed.
• The final result shows how many files were changed, how many failed and the total number of replacements. It is best to check with Count matches first and keep Back up ticked.
AboutStr.how.18.title: Support Tools > File Name Optimizer
AboutStr.how.18.body: Renames files and folders whose names contain special characters (non-Latin, optionally spaces and special marks) to safe names and updates the game files that refer to them (json, js, html, ks, rpy, etc.). Useful when porting a game to APK because APK builders often fail on non-Latin names. Pick the Source Folder, set the File scope (all files with special characters, including RPG Maker encrypted files, or only media assets) and the New name style (ASCII part kept), press Scan and Preview, then Rename and Update References. The optional Backup Folder keeps original copies of edited text files; every change is recorded in rename_mapping.json and can be reverted with Restore Original Names. There is also a Build Readiness Report (problem names, names clashing by letter case, formats often unsupported on Android) and a Fix reference letter case option. Scan, Apply and Restore run in the background: you can leave the screen, and with Background Processing on you get progress and completion notifications.
AboutStr.how.19.title: Support Tools > Media Asset Converter
AboutStr.how.19.body:
Converts game asset formats. The menu is in Support Tools, between File Helper Tools and Key Finder.
• Every converter has a File / Folder toggle at the top. Files can be multi-selected; Folder processes all matching files (choose Include subfolders to recurse; the structure is kept in the output folder). Output Format defaults to Follow Source (same format as each source file); if the source format is not available as an output (e.g. MP3), red text appears and you must pick a format manually.
• Compress (audio, image, video): choose Quality (1%–100% slider, 100% = no compression; the quality is compressed) or Size (estimated result size in KB; the size is targeted and must not exceed the source file size). PNG is compressed by reducing the number of colors. If the output format is the same the file is compressed directly; otherwise it is converted first, then compressed. Folder mode has an Only compress if larger than X KB option. The estimated result size is shown above the Start Conversion button; progress (percent and time left) and the result (Source vs Result size comparison) are shown below it. Folder mode exports into the output folder under the source folder's name (source "aset" + output "hasil" gives "hasil/aset/...").
• Settings sections can be expanded/collapsed by tapping their title (like the Q&A menu). Settings Presets saves and applies all converter settings (built-in presets and Last used settings are included).
• Folder mode: choose which source extensions to process (Source Extensions section); Create a sample and compare with the source (audio and image) converts one file first and shows a before/after comparison (audio is playable); Replace original files backs the original up to a _backup folder before overwriting it.
• When finished, Result Files lists every file with an Undo button (deletes the result, or restores the original from _backup), a per-extension summary, and a completion notification.
• Audio: Volume normalization (evens out loudness), Trim silence at start/end, and Keep OGG loop tags (LOOPSTART/LOOPLENGTH; written to both OGG Vorbis and OGG Opus). Image: PNG is compressed into a palette PNG (dithering option), and Round to a multiple keeps tileset sizes grid-aligned.
• Audio: M4A (AAC), OGG (Opus, Android 10+), WAV, MP3, FLAC or OGG (Vorbis); set bitrate, sample rate, mono/stereo and volume (1%–200% slider). Video files can also be a source (the audio is extracted). MP3, FLAC and OGG (Vorbis) are encoded by Java code inside the app (not Android's encoders), so they are slower than M4A/Opus on long files. Notes: MP3 supports only 8000–48000 Hz and standard bitrates (values are rounded to the nearest); FLAC is lossless (bitrate is unused) and slightly larger than flac -3; OGG (Vorbis) always uses 44100 or 48000 Hz and stereo (mono sources are duplicated to two channels). Choose OGG (Vorbis) for looping BGM in RPGM MV/MZ and Ren'Py because the loop tags are written.
• Image: PNG, JPG or WebP; set Resolution (Original, Percent with a 1%–100% slider, or Size Width × Height in px with Keep source aspect ratio), rotation and the JPG background for transparent images.
• Video: MP4 (H.264 or H.265) or WebM (VP9); set resolution, bitrate (dropdown, default Auto), frame rate and audio. It can take a long time; keep the app open.
• Mixed Assets: Folder mode only, for a folder holding audio, images and video together. Files are grouped by extension; each type has its own rules section (output format, compression, Advanced Settings) opened by tapping its title, and the switch on the right decides whether that type is processed (types missing from the folder are disabled automatically). Audio and images are processed first, video last. The Copy unrecognized files as they are option copies other files into the output folder. Text and Special are not included.
• When finished, if some results are larger than their sources a Discard larger results button appears (with confirmation); the Cancel button during a run also asks for confirmation.
• Special Assets: Circus .pcm (XPCM) audio to OGG/WAV and Circus .crx images to PNG (differential CRX is merged with its base image). Each converter also has per-engine presets (RPGM, Ren'Py, Kirikiri).
• Text Encoding: Shift-JIS/GBK/Big5/EUC-KR/EUC-JP to UTF-8 or back, with BOM, line ending and invalid-character options. Folder mode only processes the extensions you enter.
• Input Format and Output Format options are sorted A–Z ("All Available Formats" and "Follow Source" stay on top). Long explanations across the app are packed into a "See details (?)" link; tap it to open, tap anywhere to close.
• After a conversion, Check Compatibility compares the results with the target engine's rules (format, file names, image size, text encoding). In Overwrite Originals mode a Repack this folder button jumps straight to Pack.
• If the result file exists: Rename, Overwrite or Skip. Results are written to the output folder; source files are never changed.
AboutStr.how.20.title: Key Finder
AboutStr.how.20.body:
Finds the game encryption key.
• Open Key Finder on the main menu (or the Key Finder item in the Siglus Engine, Kirikiri, CatSystem 2, EntisGLS and RPGM MV/MZ engine menus).
• Pick the game folder, then press Analyze.
• Result: the key, the file it was found in, its status (Verified or Candidate) and the list of files encrypted with that key (50 per page). Press Copy key and paste it into the Key option of Unpack/Pack Archive.
• Supported: Siglus Engine (recovered from Scene.pck), RPGM MV/MZ (System.json or PNG header), Kirikiri XP3 (1-byte XOR key). Keys that are obfuscated or assembled at run time cannot be found unless the data itself gives a hint.
• A .txt report export is at the bottom of the results.
AboutStr.how.21.title: Support Tools > File Inspection > Duplicate File Finder
AboutStr.how.21.body:
Finds identical files in a folder and its subfolders.
• Pick a folder; the app groups files by size and then compares their content with SHA-256 (with progress and a Cancel button).
• Results are shown per group. By default every file in a group is selected except one; tap a file to change the selection. One file in each group always stays.
• The Delete button permanently deletes the selected files after a confirmation.
AboutStr.how.22.title: Support Tools > File Inspection > Hex Viewer
AboutStr.how.22.body:
Views raw file content by offset.
• Pick a file; content is shown 128 rows per page with offset, hex and ASCII columns (8 or 16 bytes per row). The go-to offset (hex) field with Go, the search mode and box, and the Find button sit above the content; page navigation « ‹ › » (first, back, next, last) is below the Find button and below the content.
• Search: type text (UTF-8 or Shift-JIS) or hex bytes (e.g. 4D 5A 90). Find next continues from the previous hit and shows the hit on the first row.
AboutStr.how.23.title: Support Tools > File Toolkit > File Cutter
AboutStr.how.23.body:
Takes part of a large file as a small file, e.g. to send as a sample.
• Pick the source file, then the part to take: Start, Middle (from the offset you enter) or End.
• Enter the amount to take and its unit (B, KB or MB). In Middle mode the start offset uses the same unit.
• The result is saved to the Output Folder (follows the Default Output Folder if set). The source file is not changed.
AboutStr.how.24.title: Support Tools > File Toolkit > File Splitter
AboutStr.how.24.body:
Splits one large file into numbered parts (.001, .002, etc.), e.g. so it can be sent or uploaded.
• Pick the source file, then how to split: By size (size of each part in KB/MB) or By part count. The number of parts that will be made is shown before you run it (maximum 9999 parts).
• The Create checksum option (on by default) writes a name.sha256 file with the SHA-256 of every part and of the whole file, which File Joiner uses to verify the result.
• The base name can be changed; results are named name.001, name.002, etc. and saved to the Output Folder. The source file is not changed.
AboutStr.how.25.title: Support Tools > File Toolkit > File Joiner
AboutStr.how.25.body:
The reverse of File Splitter: joins numbered parts (.001, .002, etc.) back into one file.
• Pick parts manually (long-press a file in the file picker to select several), or pick a folder: every numbered part set inside is detected automatically (one level) and can be joined in one go.
• The order follows the number at the end of the name, not the order you picked them. The app checks that the parts belong to one file, have no duplicate numbers and no missing numbers; if something is wrong the message is shown and the join button stays disabled.
• If a .sha256 file is available (picked together with the parts, or found in the folder), the result is verified automatically and the outcome is shown when done.
• The result is saved to the Output Folder using the parts' base name (the name can be changed for a manual pick).
AboutStr.how.26.title: Support Tools > File Toolkit > Batch Rename
AboutStr.how.26.body:
Renames many files in one folder at once.
• Pick the folder, choose this folder only or including subfolders, then (optionally) enter the extensions to process, e.g. png, jpg.
• Choose a rule: Find & Replace (on the name without extension), Number Pattern (a pattern with {nama} and {no}; start number, digit count, numbering restarts in each folder), Prefix/Suffix, or Fix Garbled Names. Letters can be made lowercase or uppercase. The file extension is always kept.
• Fix Garbled Names repairs file names garbled (e.g. ƒXƒNƒŠƒvƒg) by a wrong encoding when extracting archives: pick the encoding the names were wrongly read as and the encoding they should be (Shift-JIS, GBK, Big5, EUC-KR, UTF-8). Folder names are not repaired.
• The preview shows old and new names, 50 files per page (use ‹ ›), with a search box that filters the view by old name, new name or folder. Names that clash or are invalid are marked red and the Rename button stays disabled until fixed.
• After applying, the Undo button restores the previous names.
AboutStr.how.27.title: VN Tools > Siglus Engine
AboutStr.how.27.body:
Workflow for SiglusEngine games.
• Unpack Scene.pck via Engine List > Siglus Engine (or auto-detect). The result holds scene .dat files and _FuruArc_Siglus.meta (do not delete it).
• The Scene.pck exe key is found automatically from the scene data and stored in _FuruArc_Siglus.meta, so you need not fill it. An encrypted Gameexe.dat needs the key: get it from Key Finder and paste it into the Key option.
• Export Text on the scene .dat files, translate, then Import Text.
• Pack Archive in Siglus Engine builds a new Scene.pck from the same folder. Gameexe.dat (as Gameexe.ini) and OVK voice files can be unpacked/packed too.
• Texts are picked by filtering non-ASCII strings, so some internal strings may show up.
AboutStr.how.28.title: VN Tools > Script Tools
AboutStr.how.28.body:
Works on scripts; the type is detected per file (.rpy, .ks, .s, .cst, .dat Siglus, .bin Escu:de, .hcb, .ws2, .mes (Silky/Circus), BGI, .csx EntisGLS, .bin NeXAS, .txt).
• Export Script Text: collects dialogue and choices from all scripts in a folder into one CSV, TXT or JSON file.
• Import Script Text: writes translations back into the scripts.
• Script Contents List: writes every file name inside an archive to a text file.
Engine-specific tools (e.g. rpyc → rpy, nscript.dat decode) are under Engine List.
• Export Script Text also defaults to TXT and shows a Translate text button in its result.
AboutStr.how.29.title: VN Tools > Engine List
AboutStr.how.29.body:
All supported engines (A–Z). Tap one for Unpack/Pack specific to that engine and its script tools. NeXAS (.pac): list/extract/pack (index Huffman+XOR, zlib) and .bin script text; LZSS/zstd variants are not supported yet.
• Engine names: Adv32 (Circus), FVP (Favorite) and Softpal ADV System use the engine name. Escu:de and HexenHaus still use the developer name because their engine name is unknown. Circus has no other engine: older titles use Adv32, newer ones use Kirikiri or NeXAS (use that engine's menu).
AboutStr.how.30.title: RPGM Tools > Assets
AboutStr.how.30.body:
• Decrypt Assets: turns .rpgmvp/.rpgmvo/.rpgmvm (MV) or .png_/.ogg_/.m4a_ (MZ) back into normal files.
• Encrypt Assets: the reverse; System.json in the output is updated with the key.
• Unpack/Pack RGSS archives (XP .rgssad, VX .rgss2a, VX Ace .rgss3a).
• Decrypt/Encrypt: choose File (several allowed) or Folder with the toggle above the input field.
AboutStr.how.31.title: RPGM Tools > Translation
AboutStr.how.31.body:
• Export Text: collects dialogue and names from data/*.json into one file (CSV, TXT or JSON).
• Import Text: writes translations back. Choose the same data folder you exported from, or the data folder itself to overwrite.
• The default export format is TXT (CSV or JSON can be chosen). When Export Text finishes, the Translate text button opens the Translation Editor with the exported file already loaded.
AboutStr.how.32.title: RPGM Tools > Cheat / Save
AboutStr.how.32.body:
• Export Save turns a save file into editable JSON, Import Save turns it back.
• Value Editor edits gold, characters, items, variables and switches directly in a save.
AboutStr.how.33.title: RPGM Tools > Plugin Manager
AboutStr.how.33.body:
Manage RPG Maker MV/MZ plugins. Four tools:
• Plugin Scanner: pick the js/plugins folder (the game or js folder also works; plugins.js is optional for parameters) and press Scan. View all information lists every plugin with search and 50 per page. The Plugin Editing Area holds non-ASCII texts in code, annotation texts (@plugindesc, @text, @desc), code defaults, @default values and plugins.js parameters. Fill only the fields to change, pick an output folder and press Apply; only changed files are written and old files are kept as .bak. Texts can be exported (CSV/TXT/JSON) and their translation imported back.
• Plugin.js Editor: upload plugins.js, browse the list (search, Enabled/Disabled filter, 50 per page), tap a plugin for the Enabled switch, Up/Down load order and Remove from list. Upload New Plugin then Add Plugin. An optional plugin folder gives dependency warnings (@base, @orderAfter, @orderBefore). Profiles store and apply each plugin's enabled state. Save Plugin.js writes plugins.js to the output folder (automatic .bak backup) and copies new plugins to a plugins/ subfolder.
• Plugin Checker: match plugins.js against the plugin folder (duplicate names, missing files, unregistered files, empty files, dependencies and order).
• plugins.js Comparer: compare two versions (added, removed, status, parameters, order).
• In Plugin.js Editor: View Warnings opens a warnings page (50 per page); tap a plugin then View Parameters to edit parameter values (50 rows per page); Upload New Plugin appears after plugins.js is uploaded.
AboutStr.how.34.title: Translation Editor
AboutStr.how.34.body:
Support Tools tab > Translation Editor. Opens an export (CSV/TXT/JSON) from RPGM or VN so you can translate inside the app.
• All / Empty / Filled filter, search and jump to the next empty field.
• Editor Settings: first letter, auto wrap, replace words. Glossary and auto-fill identical entries.
• Undo bulk changes (up to 10 steps). A warning shows when control codes differ from the original.
• Save back in the same format.
• Globe icon = Online Translation (full page): Translation Service (Lingva Translate Free with no API key, or Use API Key: Google, DeepL, Gemini, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Claude, Groq, Custom; the model is picked from a dropdown and can be loaded from your account), Translation Languages, Translation Rows (empty fields / this page / all rows) and its own glossary. Parts without letters (sound effects/expressions) are filled with the Original Text when that option is on. Control codes are protected automatically; rows that lose a code are skipped and can be retried with "Retry failed". LLM providers get a language style, context notes and an option to send the 3 previous rows as context. There is also Test connection, parallel requests, a result cache, auto line wrap and an automatic glossary generator. In the row list, the "Online" filter shows results you have not edited yet. Needs internet.
AboutStr.how.35.title: File Inspection (main menu)
AboutStr.how.35.body: Contains four inspection tools, all offline. At the bottom of every report, a button copies the report or exports it to a .txt file.
AboutStr.how.36.title: File Inspection > Archive & Script
AboutStr.how.36.body:
Pick one archive or script (VN or RPGM).
• The banner above the results: green = healthy, yellow = warnings, red = problems.
• Archive: format, engine, file count, format match, duplicate names. Archive Contents browses the files, Unpack this archive opens the Unpack screen directly.
• Compute Checksum shows CRC32/MD5/SHA-256. Paste a hash from the source site into the "Match" field to be sure the download is intact.
• Check Integrity extracts every file to an empty sink to find corrupt files.
• Script: size, type, engine, encoding, encrypted or not, and wrong code or tags.
• Unrecognised files show a guess of the engine from their extension.
• When the content reads as text, the View content as text button opens a paged preview screen (50 KB per page) that can be copied page by page.
AboutStr.how.37.title: File Inspection > Folder
AboutStr.how.37.body:
Pick a game folder. Every archive and script inside is checked in turn (index and file start only, so it is fast; plain images, audio and video are skipped).
• The list is sorted with problems first. Filters: All, !, ✕, ✓.
• Tap a file for its full result; Back returns to the list.
• Export .txt saves a summary of the whole folder.
AboutStr.how.38.title: File Inspection > Compare
AboutStr.how.38.body:
Pick File A (old) and File B (new) of the same kind.
• Two archives: files added, changed, removed and same, with filter and search. Fast mode compares names and sizes, Thorough mode also compares the content of same-size files (slower).
• Two scripts/text files: number of added and removed lines (line order is ignored).
• Two translation files: new, removed entries, changed originals and changed translations.
• Other binary files: compared by size and hash.
AboutStr.how.39.title: File Inspection > Translation Scan
AboutStr.how.39.body: Pick a translation export (CSV/TXT/JSON) from RPGM or VN. Results: filled and empty entries, control codes that differ from the original, lines longer than the chosen limit, translations equal to the original, and inconsistent translations (same original, different translation). Tap a category to see its entries.
AboutStr.how.40.title: Guide
AboutStr.how.40.body: How to Use, Q&A and Troubleshooting. The Source (references and their links) and About menus are in the Settings tab. The About menu has contact, donation, Report a Problem (an email with app and device info filled in, last log optional), and Licences and Thanks.
AboutStr.how.41.title: Settings
AboutStr.how.41.body:
Settings tab. Tool Settings are shown right at the top and save automatically when changed. App Settings opens from its menu; every change is applied and saved automatically.
• Tool Settings: what to do when a file already exists on export (Overwrite, Skip, Rename) and the Default Output Folder used when no Output Folder is chosen.
• Display settings: theme mode (Follow system, Light, Dark; default Follow system) and theme colour.
• Language settings: Follow system (default), English, Japanese, Chinese, Korean or Indonesian. If the system language is not supported, English is used. Japanese, Chinese and Korean currently cover only part of the interface (main menu, settings and Game Assets); the rest is shown in English. Kanji/hanzi/hangul use the system font.
• System settings: Engine label on Game Assets covers (off by default), Background Processing (keeps running when the app is closed or the screen is off, with a notification), Keep screen on while running, Confirm exit for the Translation Editor and Value Editor (asks first when there are unsaved changes), and Native text input (uses Android's built-in text fields to avoid bugs).
AboutStr.how.42.title: Tips
AboutStr.how.42.body:
• Always keep a copy of the original archive or folder before overwriting.
• For big archives keep the screen on or enable background processing.
• If extracted file names look garbled, change the filename encoding (Shift-JIS, UTF-8, GBK, etc.).
AboutStr.qna.1.title: Does this app need internet?
AboutStr.qna.1.body: Only for three features: (1) Online Translation in the Translation Editor (globe icon), (2) online cover search in Game Assets (Auto search / Manual search / cloud icon; sources are VNDB, NextMoe, Steam and Bing), and (3) Check for updates: the app reads the latest release on GitHub (automatically when the app opens if you are online, or via Settings > Check for updates; only the version number and release notes are read, no personal data is sent, and the download opens in your browser). For cover search only the game name is sent to those sites, then the chosen image is downloaded and kept in the app storage. Without internet you can still pick a cover from a file on the device or have it taken from inside the game folder. All unpacking, packing, text export/import, inspection and asset browsing still run offline on your device. Text translated online is sent to the provider you choose (Lingva, Google, DeepL, Gemini, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Claude, Groq or a Custom URL); API keys are stored on the device only. Links in the Source and About menus are opened by your browser.
AboutStr.qna.2.title: Why are some developer names in the Engine List?
AboutStr.qna.2.body: Some games are recognised by their developer's archive format. When the engine name is known the list uses it with the developer in brackets, e.g. Adv32 (Circus) or FVP (Favorite). When it is not known (Escu:de, HexenHaus), the developer name is used. One developer can use different engines per title; if a game does not match, try another engine (e.g. Kirikiri or NeXAS for newer Circus titles).
AboutStr.qna.3.title: How does the app recognise an archive format?
AboutStr.qna.3.body: By the signature (magic bytes) at the start of the file, and for formats without one by checking the structure. If it is not recognised, try Engine List when you know the engine.
AboutStr.qna.4.title: Why are extracted file names garbled?
AboutStr.qna.4.body: Names inside the archive use a specific encoding (usually Shift-JIS). Change the Filename encoding option; the file list reloads automatically.
AboutStr.qna.5.title: How do I get the key for Siglus Gameexe.dat?
AboutStr.qna.5.body: For Scene.pck you need not: the key is found automatically from the scene data. For Gameexe.dat, open Key Finder on the game folder (with Scene.pck), copy the key and paste it into the Key option. The Siglus key is not stored whole in SiglusEngine.exe (it is assembled at run time), so it is derived from the scene data.
AboutStr.qna.6.title: What is the XOR key in archive options?
AboutStr.qna.6.body: Some games disguise archive contents with a single-byte XOR. The app tries to detect it; if that fails, enter the key (hex) manually.
AboutStr.qna.7.title: Full unpack vs Select Files?
AboutStr.qna.7.body: Full unpack extracts everything. Select Files lets you tick only certain files or folders, which is faster and saves space.
AboutStr.qna.8.title: How do I translate an RPGM game?
AboutStr.qna.8.body: Export Text → translate in the Translation Editor (or any editor) → Import Text into the data folder. Replace the game's data with the result.
AboutStr.qna.9.title: How do I translate a visual novel?
AboutStr.qna.9.body: Unpack the script archive → Export Script Text → translate → Import Script Text → Pack Archive if the game reads from an archive (or put the files in the game folder).
AboutStr.qna.10.title: What are the control-code warnings in the editor?
AboutStr.qna.10.body: Codes like \C[2], \N[1] or script tags must stay in the translation so colours, names and pauses remain correct. The editor warns when they differ from the original.
AboutStr.qna.11.title: What is File Inspection for and which tool should I use?
AboutStr.qna.11.body: One file → Archive & Script Inspection. A whole game folder → Folder Inspection. Two versions of a file (e.g. before and after an update) → Compare Files. A translation export → Translation Scan.
AboutStr.qna.12.title: How do I make sure my downloaded archive is not corrupt?
AboutStr.qna.12.body: In Archive & Script Inspection press Compute Checksum, then paste the hash (CRC32, MD5 or SHA-256) from the source site into the Match field. A ✓ appears when it matches. If the source gives no hash, use Check Integrity.
AboutStr.qna.13.title: What is the difference between Check extracted files and Check packing integrity?
AboutStr.qna.13.body: Check extracted files (after Unpack) compares the output with the archive: size, and the checksum when the archive stores one (XP3), or a re-extraction in memory for other formats. Check packing integrity (after Pack) reads the new archive back and compares each file with the source folder.
AboutStr.qna.14.title: Folder Inspection stops at 5000 files, how do I continue?
AboutStr.qna.14.body: Inspection runs in batches of 5000 files. When it finishes, tap Continue with the next batch to check the rest. The summary (size, file count, engine) always covers the whole folder.
AboutStr.qna.15.title: Does Folder Inspection modify or move files?
AboutStr.qna.15.body: No. All inspections are read-only. Nothing in the folder is changed.
AboutStr.qna.16.title: Does the Plugin Scanner change my original plugins?
AboutStr.qna.16.body: No. Results go to the output folder; if a file with the same name already exists there, the old copy is kept as .bak. The Plugin.js Editor works the same way. Copy the result into the game folder yourself when you are sure.
AboutStr.qna.17.title: Why does a @default value not change the game?
AboutStr.qna.17.body: @default in the annotation is only the default shown by the RPG Maker editor. The values the game uses live in plugins.js (parameters) or in code defaults (e.g. parameters['x'] || 10); both can be edited in the Plugin Scanner.
AboutStr.qna.18.title: Why does Compare say "same" although the archive content differs?
AboutStr.qna.18.body: Fast mode only compares file names and sizes inside the archive, so different content of the same size is not detected. Use Thorough mode to compare content too.
AboutStr.qna.19.title: What is in the .txt report and where can I open it?
AboutStr.qna.19.body: Plain text with the status, information, findings and checksums (or the list of differences). Open it in any text editor and send it to the game creator or the developer when reporting.
AboutStr.qna.20.title: What does the "too long" warning in Translation Scan mean?
AboutStr.qna.20.body: Some translation lines are longer than the limit you chose (control codes are not counted), so they may be cut off in the game dialog box. Adjust them with auto wrap in the Translation Editor.
AboutStr.qna.21.title: Are my original files modified?
AboutStr.qna.21.body: No, unless you deliberately choose an output folder equal to the source (e.g. Import Text into the data folder). The app works on copies in the output folder.
AboutStr.qna.22.title: What is Check Integrity and why is it slow?
AboutStr.qna.22.body: It extracts every file of the archive to an empty sink and compares checksums when available, so corrupt files are found. It is as slow as extracting the whole archive.
AboutStr.qna.23.title: A script check says "may be wrong". Is it broken?
AboutStr.qna.23.body: Not necessarily. Script checks are heuristic (e.g. unpaired quotes, incomplete if/endif tags). Treat them as warnings to verify manually.
AboutStr.qna.24.title: Siglus Scene.pck fails to unpack, or Pack Archive asks for the .meta file
AboutStr.qna.24.body: If it says a key is needed, fill the Key option. Pack Archive needs the _FuruArc_Siglus.meta created when unpacking; unpack the original Scene.pck first and edit the resulting folder (do not delete the .meta file).
AboutStr.qna.25.title: Why is my game not recognised or fails to unpack?
AboutStr.qna.25.body: The archive may use a game-specific key, be truncated from a bad download, or use a format version that is not supported yet. Use Archive & Script Inspection to see the cause.
AboutStr.qna.26.title: Is it OK to unpack copyrighted games?
AboutStr.qna.26.body: Only use it on games you own, for personal purposes such as translation or modding, and follow the game creator's rules.
AboutStr.qna.27.title: How do I report a problem or suggest something?
AboutStr.qna.27.body: Contact the developer via Settings tab > About (email or Github).
AboutStr.qna.28.title: Why does text look garbled in the Text Editor?
AboutStr.qna.28.body: The file encoding may not have been detected correctly. Open Options > Encoding & Line Endings, choose the right encoding (e.g. Shift-JIS, GBK, Big5 or EUC-KR), then press Reload with this encoding. Older visual novel scripts often use Shift-JIS.
AboutStr.qna.29.title: Why does the Text Editor refuse to save?
AboutStr.qna.29.body: Two common causes: some characters cannot be saved in the chosen encoding (choose UTF-8 under Save as), or the JSON in the Text view is invalid (fix it according to the error message). Also make sure an Output Folder is picked, or choose Overwrite Originals under Upload File.
AboutStr.qna.30.title: Does the Text Editor change my original files?
AboutStr.qna.30.body: Only if you choose Overwrite Originals under Upload File. With Back up ticked, the original is first copied to the _backup folder inside the Output Folder. With Output Folder, the original is not touched.
AboutStr.qna.31.title: Why do the CSV columns look shifted or merged?
AboutStr.qna.31.body: The column separator may have been guessed wrongly. Open Options > CSV Settings and choose the right Column separator (Comma, Semicolon, Tab or Pipe), then open the Encoding & Line Endings section and press Reload with this encoding.
AboutStr.qna.32.title: Are comments in an INI file lost when I edit it in Structured Text?
AboutStr.qna.32.body: No. The INI editor only rewrites the lines you change, add or delete. Comments, blank lines and the rest of the order stay as they were.
AboutStr.qna.33.title: Are my changes lost if the app closes before I save?
AboutStr.qna.33.body: Not necessarily. The editor writes an automatic draft 2 seconds after the last change. When you open the same file again you are offered Restore. The draft is deleted after a successful save or when you choose Leave without saving.
